subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Stepper Motors: Precision in Steps
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Stepper Motors: Precision in Steps.

hook.text: A stepper motor moves in exact, repeatable clicks — not continuous rotation.

buildup.text: Multiple coils energize in sequence. Each pulse moves the rotor one precise step.

discovery.text: A typical stepper divides one revolution into 200 steps — 1.8° per step.

twist.text: Microstepping drives subdivide each step further — 256 microsteps give ultra-smooth motion.

climax.text: 3D printers, CNC machines, and telescope mounts rely on stepper motor precision.

punchline.text: One pulse, one step — perfect position control without a sensor.

quiz.question: How does a stepper motor achieve precise positioning?
options: It uses a built-in encoder to measure position
It moves in fixed angular steps — one per electrical pulse
It adjusts speed based on back-EMF feedback
